title.en: UNION, INTERSECT, MINUS and Cartesian product

body.en: Set operations need union-compatible relations (same number of attributes, matching domains). UNION gives tuples in either relation, without duplicates. INTERSECT gives tuples common to both. MINUS (EXCEPT in standard SQL) gives tuples in the first but not in the second. The Cartesian product pairs every tuple of one relation with every tuple of the other: its degree is the sum and its cardinality is the product.

points.en: MINUS / EXCEPT: in A, not in B
A × B: degree = d₁ + d₂, cardinality = n₁ × n₂

narration.en: UNION combines, INTERSECT keeps common tuples, MINUS keeps tuples only in the first. A Cartesian product adds degrees and multiplies cardinalities.
narration.kn: UNION ಸಂಯೋಜಿಸುತ್ತದೆ, INTERSECT ಸಾಮಾನ್ಯ ಟ್ಯೂಪಲ್ ಉಳಿಸುತ್ತದೆ, MINUS ಮೊದಲದರಲ್ಲಿ ಮಾತ್ರ ಇರುವವು. ಕಾರ್ಟೀಸಿಯನ್ ಗುಣಲಬ್ಧದಲ್ಲಿ ಡಿಗ್ರಿ ಕೂಡುತ್ತವೆ, ಕಾರ್ಡಿನಾಲಿಟಿ ಗುಣಿಸುತ್ತವೆ.

body.en: A JOIN combines tuples of two relations that satisfy a condition, usually equality of a common attribute (an equi-join). It can be written as a Cartesian product with a WHERE condition, or with JOIN ... ON. Table aliases (STUDENT S) keep the query short; columns with the same name are written as S.RollNo and F.RollNo.

points.en: Or: STUDENT S JOIN FEES F ON S.RollNo = F.RollNo
Without a join condition you get the full Cartesian product

narration.en: A join matches rows of two tables on a common column, such as roll number. Without the join condition, you get every possible pair of rows.
narration.kn: ಜೋಡಣೆ ಎರಡು ಕೋಷ್ಟಕಗಳ ಸಾಲುಗಳನ್ನು ಕ್ರಮಸಂಖ್ಯೆಯಂತಹ ಸಾಮಾನ್ಯ ಕಾಲಂ ಮೇಲೆ ಹೊಂದಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. ಷರತ್ತು ಇಲ್ಲದಿದ್ದರೆ ಎಲ್ಲ ಸಾಧ್ಯ ಜೋಡಿಗಳು ಬರುತ್ತವೆ.

problem.en: DANCE(SNo, Name, Class) has (1, Aastha, 7A), (2, Mahira, 6A), (3, Mohit, 7B), (4, Sanjay, 7A). MUSIC has (1, Mehak, 8A), (2, Mahira, 6A), (3, Lavanya, 7A), (4, Sanjay, 7A), (5, Abhay, 8A). Find who is in both clubs, and the size of DANCE × MUSIC.

steps.en: SELECT Name, Class FROM DANCE INTERSECT SELECT Name, Class FROM MUSIC;
SELECT Name, Class FROM DANCE EXCEPT SELECT Name, Class FROM MUSIC; gives Aastha 7A and Mohit 7B (MINUS in the textbook).

answer.en: Both clubs: Mahira, Sanjay. DANCE × MUSIC has degree 6 and 20 tuples.

narration.en: Let us work through this together. DANCE(SNo, Name, Class) has (1, Aastha, 7A), (2, Mahira, 6A), (3, Mohit, 7B), (4, Sanjay, 7A). MUSIC has (1, Mehak, 8A), (2, Mahira, 6A), (3, Lavanya, 7A), (4, Sanjay, 7A), (5, Abhay, 8A). Find who is in both clubs, and the size of DANCE × MUSIC.

problem.en: STUDENT as before and FEES(RollNo, Term, Amount) = (1, 1, 15000), (3, 1, 15000), (3, 2, 12000), (6, 1, 15000). Show each payer's name and total fee paid.

steps.en: SELECT S.SName, SUM(F.Amount) FROM STUDENT S JOIN FEES F ON S.RollNo = F.RollNo GROUP BY S.SName;
